content_zh:
北境冰原！
永恒冻土！
每一次踩踏这片土地都带着刺骨的寒意，巴顿裹紧了身上那件厚实的兽皮甲，浑浊的眼珠警惕地扫过村口那片死寂的白茫茫。
更远处一道灰白色的巨墙横亘在地平线上，那是连绵数千公里，万年冰封的雪山，它的余脉向西延伸，被一片浓得化不开的墨绿色吞噬。
那是紧贴着山脚生长的怪树林，即使在最凛冽的寒冬，那些异常高大的粗壮树木，也闪烁着近乎金属的冷光，透着难以言喻的诡异。
“这该死的鬼天气，骨头缝都冻透了……”
阿伦嘟囔着，跺了跺脚。
巴顿没接话，光依旧注视着这片土地，这里资源匮乏，北方是凡人无法企及的神只雪山，西南方的怪树林是怪物的猎场，唯一看似通行的东南道路，盘踞着比野兽更凶残的强盗、逃兵。
铁皮村，这个挤在雪山与怪林夹角处微末村落，世代谨守着一个铁律‘容不下外来者’，每一个闯入者，都是对有限生存资源的掠夺。
“嘿！
又是他！”
阿伦的斥骂声骤然响起，“这该死的小偷，昨天才在磨坊边鬼鬼祟祟，今天还敢来！”
巴顿猛地转头，浑浊的眼睛锁定了村口不远处一个隆起的雪堆，雪堆后一个瘦得像骷髅的身影正缩着脖子，那身破烂的布片在寒风中根本挡不住一丝寒意。
是那个一月前突然出现在村外，像幽灵一样徘徊的乞丐。
阿伦立刻挺直腰板，石矛指向雪堆：“滚出来！
臭乞丐！
再敢靠近，老子打断你的狗腿！”
巴顿没说话，布满老茧的手无声地按在了腰间短柄石斧上，眼底闪过一丝微不可察的怜悯。
收留是不可能的，驱逐已是最大的仁慈，虽然这仁慈也意味着死亡。
“等等！

两位英勇的骑士老爷！”
凯撒连忙从雪堆后钻出来。
“我是来道歉的！
为我之前鲁莽行为，向两位骑士老爷郑重道歉！”
凯撒刻意咬重了骑士老爷四个字。
阿伦的神色缓和了一丝，这片被遗忘的冻土角落没有文明，这个遥远尊贵的称谓无比遥远，哪怕明知是奉承，但也带来一丝短暂的虚荣。
巴顿叹了口气，浑浊的目光扫过凯撒：“孩子！
听我说，铁皮村的规矩，是刻在骨头里的，这片冻土养活自己人都要拼尽全力，实在容不下外人了。”
巴顿摇摇头，声音低沉下去:“趁还能走，往……往你觉得有活路的地方去。”
他话没说完，但意思明确，哪条路都是绝路。
“两位骑士老爷言重了！”
content_en:
Northern ice fields!
Eternal frozen soil!
Every time he stepped on the land, there was a biting chill. Barton wrapped himself tightly in the thick animal skin armor, and his turbid eyes vigilantly scanned the dead white at the entrance of the village.
Farther away, a huge gray-white wall stretches across the horizon. It is a snow-capped mountain that stretches for thousands of kilometers and has been frozen for ten thousand years. Its remaining veins extend to the west and are swallowed up by a dark green that is so thick that it cannot be dissolved.
It was a strange forest growing close to the foot of the mountain. Even in the harshest winter, those unusually tall and thick trees shone with an almost metallic cold light, revealing an indescribable weirdness.
"This damn weather, my bones are frozen to the bone..."
Allen muttered and stamped his feet.
Barton didn't answer, and Guang still stared at this land. There were few resources here. In the north were the divine snow-capped mountains that were beyond the reach of mortals. The strange woods in the southwest were the hunting ground of monsters. The only southeast road that seemed to be passable was occupied by bandits and deserters who were more ferocious than wild beasts.
Tiebi Village, a tiny village squeezed between the snow-capped mountains and strange forests, has adhered to an iron law for generations, "No outsiders allowed." Every intruder is a plunder of limited survival resources.
"Hey!
It's him again! "
Allen's scolding suddenly sounded, "This damn thief was sneaking around the mill yesterday, and he dares to come here today!"
Barton turned his head suddenly, his turbid eyes locked on a raised snowdrift not far from the village entrance. Behind the snowdrift, a figure as thin as a skeleton was shrinking his neck. The tattered cloth could not block the chill in the cold wind.
It was the beggar who suddenly appeared outside the village a month ago, wandering like a ghost.
Allen immediately straightened his back and pointed his stone spear at the snowdrift: "Get out!
Stinky beggar!
If you dare to get close again, I will break your legs! "
Barton said nothing, his calloused hands silently pressed on the short-handled stone ax at his waist, and a trace of imperceptible pity flashed in his eyes.
Inclusion is impossible, expulsion is the greatest mercy, although this mercy also means death.
"Wait!
Two brave knights! "
Caesar quickly emerged from behind the snowdrift.
"I'm here to apologize!
I solemnly apologize to the two knights for my previous reckless behavior! "
Caesar deliberately emphasized the word knight.
Allen's expression softened a little. There was no civilization in this forgotten corner of the frozen land. This distant and noble title was extremely far away. Even though he knew it was flattery, it still brought a trace of short-term vanity.
Barton sighed and glanced at Caesar with his turbid eyes: "Child!
Listen to me, the rules of Ironhide Village are engraved in the bones. People in this frozen land have to work hard to feed themselves, and there is really no room for outsiders. "
Barton shook his head and his voice deepened: "While you can still go, go... to where you think there is a way to survive."
He didn't finish his words, but his meaning was clear, no matter which way he went, it would be a dead end.
"The two knights spoke seriously!"
